summary: D.C.'s new delegate is working to build congressional support for statehood as advocates highlight the District's population size relative to existing states and document what they describe as repeated congressional incursions into local authority, including recent concerns about National Guard deployment in the capital. Without statehood, D.C. residents have no senators, and their one delegate to the House cannot vote on the House floor.
